- Corn stalk/leaf sheath tissue that has turned tan/yellowish-brown (senescent)
- Densely scattered tiny black dots distributed randomly across the surface
- The dots appear embedded in the tissue (not powdery/wipeable)

**Comparison with reference images:**
- **Tar spot**: The bottom-right panel of the Tar spot reference shows the exact same pattern — tan/brownish leaf or sheath tissue densely covered with tiny black stromata. This is a near-perfect match.
- **Physoderma brown spot**: Bottom-right shows black dots too, but on green tissue and the dots tend to cluster near midrib
- **Diplodia stalk rot**: Has pycnidia near nodes but the reference images show different tissue morphology
- **Charcoal stalk rot**: Shows shredded internal pith with sclerotia on vascular strands, not scattered dots on intact outer surface

The scattered tiny black raised structures (stromata) on tan/brown stalk/sheath tissue is the hallmark of Tar spot — "raised black tar-like spots that cannot be wiped or rubbed off." The bottom-right panel of the Tar spot collage matches the test image almost exactly.
